projects.title: FoodSpace
projects.cardDescription: A MERN-based food marketplace connecting local home cooks with nearby buyers, promoting zero food waste and 0% platform commission.
projects.pageDescription:
FoodSpace is a full-stack web application inspired by platforms like Zomato and Swiggy, built to empower local home cooks and reduce food waste. The platform enables individuals to sell freshly prepared homemade food to nearby users without any platform fees. Buyers can browse food listings based on their primary location and a configurable distance range, while sellers have complete control over menu visibility, pricing, and availability.

The application focuses on transparency and decentralization — sellers receive payments directly, and the platform does not act as an intermediary for delivery. Each seller is responsible for fulfilling and delivering their own orders, ensuring trust and accountability.

From a technical perspective, FoodSpace includes secure JWT-based authentication, role-based access for buyers and sellers, location-aware listings, cart and order management, and a dedicated seller dashboard. The frontend is optimized for responsiveness and usability using modern UI libraries, while the backend follows RESTful API principles for scalability and maintainability.

Due to limited resources, the application is not hosted, but the complete source code and architecture are available on GitHub.
projects.problem: Local communities face significant food waste, while talented home cooks lack a reliable platform to sell homemade food. Buyers also struggle to find authentic, nearby homemade meals at fair prices.
projects.solution: Designed and developed a transparent, commission-free marketplace using the MERN stack. Implemented location-based food discovery, seller-controlled listings, JWT-secured authentication, and a seller dashboard to enable direct buyer–seller interaction while strengthening the local food economy.

projects.title: Travel Diaries
projects.cardDescription: A privacy-focused social platform for travel enthusiasts to share guides, connect with like-minded travelers, and chat in real time.
projects.pageDescription:
Travel Diaries is a social networking web application built specifically for travel enthusiasts who want more than just photo sharing. The platform enables users to document complete travel journeys, including routes, experiences, and guidance, while fostering a responsible travel culture that respects destinations and local communities.

Users can create detailed posts, like and comment on shared experiences, and connect with individuals or groups that share similar travel interests. The application also features a real-time chat system supporting one-to-one and group conversations.

A strong emphasis is placed on user privacy and data protection. Chats are end-to-end aware in behavior — deleted messages are removed from both sides, screenshots and chat saving are restricted, and sensitive actions are safeguarded. Authentication is handled using Google OAuth 2.0 and OTP-based email verification to ensure secure onboarding.

From a technical standpoint, the application leverages the MERN stack for scalability, Socket.io for real-time communication, Firebase for secure image storage, and SMTP services for OTP delivery. Although not deployed due to resource limitations, the project demonstrates advanced full-stack, real-time, and privacy-centric application design.
projects.problem: Travelers rely on fragmented social media platforms that lack structured travel guides, meaningful connections, real-time interaction, and privacy-focused communication.
projects.solution: Built a dedicated travel social network using the MERN stack with real-time chat, OAuth-based authentication, OTP verification, and privacy-first chat controls. The platform enables structured travel storytelling, group collaboration, and secure communication.

projects.title: Route Planning Tool
projects.cardDescription: A smart route optimization tool that calculates and visualizes the shortest path across multiple destinations using Mapbox.
projects.pageDescription:
The Route Planning Tool is a web-based navigation application designed to help users efficiently plan trips involving multiple destinations. Unlike standard map applications that primarily focus on point-to-point navigation, this tool calculates an optimized route covering all selected locations with the shortest possible distance.

Users can enter their current location and add multiple destinations dynamically. The system processes these inputs using route optimization logic and visualizes the complete path on an interactive Mapbox-powered map.

As the user moves, the application updates the route in real time and automatically removes destination markers once they are reached, providing a clean and intuitive navigation experience. This makes the tool especially useful for delivery routes, travel itineraries, and multi-stop journeys.

The backend is built using Node.js and Express.js, with SQLite used for lightweight and efficient data storage. Although the application is not hosted, it demonstrates strong integration of mapping services, real-time updates, and algorithm-driven route optimization.
projects.problem: Standard navigation tools are inefficient for planning trips with multiple stops, often resulting in longer travel times and unnecessary fuel consumption.
projects.solution: Developed a smart routing application using Mapbox and Node.js that computes the shortest route across multiple destinations, visualizes it interactively, and dynamically updates the route while removing completed stops.

blogs.title: Docker Basics: Definition, Common Commands, and Dockerfile Instructions
blogs.summary: A beginner-friendly overview of Docker, covering its definition, commonly used Docker commands, container and image management, and essential Dockerfile instructions for building and running containerized applications.
blogs.fullContent:
Docker is a containerization platform that allows developers to package applications and their dependencies into lightweight, portable containers. These containers can run consistently across different environments such as development, testing, and production.

Note: For local Linux systems, use `sudo` before every Docker command.

```bash
# 1. Build a Docker Image
docker build -t image_name .
docker build -t image_name:v1.0.0 .
# Semantic Versioning: v1.0.0 -> 1 (Major), 0 (Minor), 0 (Bug Fix)

# 2. Run a Docker Image
docker run -it -p host_port:container_port image_name:v1.0.0
docker run -it -p host_port:container_port --restart=always image_name:v1.0.0

# Example with NGINX port mapping
docker run -it -p host_port:nginx_port --restart=always image_name:v1.0.0

# Interactive mode (-it)
# Detached mode (-d)
docker run -d image_name

# Inject environment variables
docker run -e ENV_VAR=value image_name

# Assign a container name
docker run -d --name first-docker-container hello-world

# Persistent volume mapping
docker run -v host_path:container_path image_name

# Note: docker run always creates a new container

# 3. Start an existing container
docker start container_id | container_name

# 4. Stop a running container
docker stop container_id

# List running containers
docker ps

# 5. List Docker images
docker images

# 6. List running containers
docker ps

# 7. List all containers (running + stopped)
docker ps -a

# 8. Remove a Docker image
docker rmi image_name
# If image is in use, stop the container first

# 9. Remove a Docker container
docker rm container_id | container_name
```

Dockerfile Instructions:

```Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine        # Base image
WORKDIR /app               # Working directory
COPY . .                   # Copy files to container
RUN npm install             # Run build commands
EXPOSE 3000                # Expose container port
ENV NODE_ENV=production    # Environment variable
CMD ["npm", "start"]     # Start application (only one CMD allowed)
```

Additional Dockerfile Instructions:

```Dockerfile
ARG VERSION=1.0
ENTRYPOINT ["node", "app.js"]
VOLUME /data
LABEL version="1.0" description="Sample Docker App"
SHELL ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
USER node
```

blogs.title: Cloud Resume Challenge – AWS (Complete Technical Guide)
blogs.summary: A comprehensive, hands-on walkthrough for the Cloud Resume Challenge on AWS. Covers everything from S3 hosting and CloudFront distribution to serverless APIs with Lambda/DynamoDB, CI/CD automation, and Infrastructure as Code.
blogs.fullContent:
The Cloud Resume Challenge is a hands-on project that demonstrates cloud proficiency by building and deploying a resume website using AWS services, incorporating infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, and modern web development practices.

CHALLENGE CHECKLIST

- Certification (Completed)
- HTML & CSS (Completed)
- Static Website (Completed)
- HTTPS & DNS (Completed)
- Javascript & Database (Completed)
- API & Python (Completed)
- Tests (Completed)
- Infrastructure as Code (Pending)
- Source Control (Completed)
- CI/CD - Front end & Back end (Completed)
- Blog post (Pending)

PART 1: CERTIFICATION
Obtain an AWS certification to validate your cloud knowledge. Recommended paths: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner or AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate.

PART 2-3: CREATE ONLINE RESUME
Build your resume using HTML/CSS or React. For this guide, we use React for modularity. 
Project Structure:
src/
  assets/common.json (Data)
  components/ (Sidebar, Hero, Experience, Education, Projects, Skills, Achievements, Footer)
  App.tsx & main.tsx (Logic & Entry)

PART 4: STATIC WEBSITE (S3)
1. Create S3 Bucket: Log in to AWS, search for S3, and create a globally unique bucket (e.g., my-resume-challenge-123).
2. Configure Public Access: Temporarily uncheck Block Public Access settings for testing.
3. Upload Files: Open the bucket, click Upload, and add your website files (HTML, CSS, JS, images).
4. Bucket Policy: Add a policy for public read access (replace YOUR-BUCKET-NAME):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "PublicReadGetObject",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::YOUR-BUCKET-NAME/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

5. Enable Hosting: In Properties, toggle Static website hosting to Enable and set Index document as index.html.

PART 5: HTTPS & DISTRIBUTION (CLOUDFRONT)
1. Create Distribution: Open CloudFront and click Create Distribution. Select your S3 bucket as the origin.
2. Configure Settings: Set Viewer Protocol Policy to Redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Set Default Root Object to index.html.
3. Update S3 Policy: Update your S3 bucket policy to allow CloudFront access (often via OAC - Origin Access Control).
4. Global Access: Once enabled, copy the Distribution Domain Name to access your site securely via HTTPS.

PART 6: DNS (ROUTE 53)
1. Hosted Zone: Create a hosted zone in Route 53 for your domain name.
2. DNS Records: Create an A-record alias pointing to your CloudFront distribution.
3. SSL Certificate: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in us-east-1 to request a public certificate for your domain and validate it via DNS.

PART 7: JAVASCRIPT & VISITOR COUNTER
Add a function to your frontend to fetch the visitor count from your API:

```javascript
useEffect(() => {
    const fetchData = async () => {
      try {
        const response = await fetch(api_url, { method: "GET" });
        const data = await response.json();
        setVisitCount(data.visitorCount);
      } catch (err) { console.error(err); }
    };
    fetchData();
}, [api_url]);
```

PART 8: DATABASE (DYNAMODB)
1. Create Table: In DynamoDB, create a table named resume-visitor-counter with partition key id (String).
2. Initial Item: Create an item with id: viewCounter and a number attribute count set to 0.

PART 9-10: API & PYTHON (LAMBDA)
1. Create Function: Create a Lambda function with Python runtime.
2. Lambda Code:

```python
import boto3
import json
from decimal import Decimal

dynamodb = boto3.resource("dynamodb")
table = dynamodb.Table("resume-visitor-counter")

def lambda_handler(event, context):
    try:
        method = event.get("httpMethod", "")
        if method.upper() != "GET":
            return {"statusCode": 405, "body": json.dumps({"error": "Method not allowed"})}

        response = table.update_item(
            Key={"id": "viewCounter"},
            UpdateExpression="SET #c = if_not_exists(#c, :start) + :inc",
            ExpressionAttributeNames={"#c": "count"},
            ExpressionAttributeValues={":inc": 1, ":start": 0},
            ReturnValues="UPDATED_NEW"
        )
        count = int(response["Attributes"]["count"])
        return {
            "statusCode": 200,
            "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*"},
            "body": json.dumps({"visitorCount": count})
        }
    except Exception as e:
        return {"statusCode": 500, "body": json.dumps({"error": str(e)})}
```

3. IAM Permissions: Attach AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess to the Lambda role.
4. Function URL: Enable a Function URL with Auth Type NONE and configure CORS for GET requests.

PART 11: TESTING
Write unit tests for your Lambda function in Python (using unittest or pytest) and for your React components (using Jest or Vitest) to ensure the visitor counter and API interactions work as expected.

PART 12: INFRASTRUCTURE AS CODE (IAC)
Use Terraform or AWS SAM to define your infrastructure. This allows you to manage S3, CloudFront, DynamoDB, and Lambda consistently through code.

PART 13-15: SOURCE CONTROL & CI/CD
1. Source Control: Push your project to GitHub.
2. CI/CD Backend: Use GitHub Actions to automate Lambda deployments on every push to the main branch.
3. CI/CD Frontend: Create a workflow to build your Vite app, sync files to S3, and invalidate CloudFront cache.

ARCHITECTURE & COSTS
The architecture follows a serverless flow: Route 53 -> CloudFront -> S3 (Static Assets) and Lambda -> DynamoDB (API Data). The entire setup is Free Tier eligible, with estimated costs of $2-3/month for domain management.

CONCLUSIONS & NEXT STEPS
Completing this challenge validates skills in cloud architecture, security, and automation. Move forward by implementing AWS WAF for security and monitoring with CloudWatch Alarms.
